framings.text: The team needs coordination that feels worthwhile and keeps people aligned without exhausting meetings.
The deeper issue may be constantly changing priorities, with visibility efforts risking surveillance rather than useful alignment.

outcome: The team feels aligned on current priorities and progress, with coordination that is focused, trusted, and worth participating in.

questions.text: Which is the deeper concern: ineffective coordination meetings, or priorities changing so often that alignment breaks down?

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: shift most updates to asynchronous participation
alternatives.benefit: Could reduce meeting time and preserve updates for people who need them.
alternatives.cost: People may stop reading, weakening shared awareness.
alternatives.undo_cost: Provisional; reverting may be straightforward but could renew meeting fatigue.

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: keep a smaller recurring live rhythm and redesign the rest of coordination around priority changes
alternatives.benefit: Could preserve face-to-face connection while focusing live time on decisions and changes.
alternatives.cost: Requires discipline about what belongs live and may not solve underlying priority instability.
alternatives.undo_cost: Provisional; the changed rhythm may be easy to reverse, but habits may persist.
